paragraphs: My name is Lily, and I am ten years old. On Friday, the weather was bad, and it rained all morning. So our class went to the town museum. The building is from the nineteenth century. It is more than a century old. It has five floors. "Today we will explore one floor at a time," said Teacher Kim. We started on the first floor at nine o'clock.

The first floor tells the history of our town. We saw old photos of the market and the river. On the second floor, there were old toys. Mia loved a wooden horse with red wheels. The third floor was the sports floor. We saw old skis, a leather ball, and a snowboard. "Can I try the snowboard?" asked Leo. "No, it is behind glass," said Teacher Kim. "Snow is very cold, and we have none here," said Mia.

The fourth floor was about animals and plants. We looked at a big butterfly and a small bird. "Is there somewhere to sit?" asked Leo. "Yes, in the garden on the fifth floor," said Teacher Kim. We went up the stairs at midday. The rain stopped, and the sky was bright. We ate lunch in the garden at twelve o'clock.

In the afternoon, we went down to the second floor. Mia asked Teacher Kim about the wooden horse. "A child made it in the nineteenth century," said Teacher Kim. At half past two, we left the museum. The bad weather was now a good day for us. Ordinal numbers help us find the floor we want. First, second, third, fourth, and fifth!
text.summary: Lily's class visits a museum with five floors. Each floor has an ordinal number, and a time in words tells when the class eats lunch.
